label: <DEL> step of long (L=8-9) sequences
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (89% of activation mass), and almost only when the sequence is long: L=9 holds about 77% of the mass and L=8 about 22%. It never fires for L<=4 and barely fires for L 5-7. Among long-sequence delimiters only about 32% fire, so precision is weak. Which ones fire depends diffusely on sequence content: rates are higher when the first token (the first one to be copied) is o, g, t, 2 or z, but no simple content rule improved F1. Smaller secondary activity: the last original token of L=9 sequences (just before <DEL>), and the first copy step(s) right after <DEL>, often z. Very rare elsewhere in the copy phase. Never fires on original steps 0-6.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: o, g, t, 2; copy phase: g, r, y, t; input phase: ) and the third original token (most: n, s, v, h, b, a; least: 2, o, 3, t); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=8, L=9.
